title: Northstar Banking Engineering Residency
warnings: All financial records are synthetic. Never use production credentials or account data.
X-Demo-User is caller-controlled and is NOT a real authentication system. Bind localhost only.
GitHub Pages is a static learning interface; code and tests run locally or in Codespaces.
Browser ticket progress and simulated reviews are not employer-verified skills.

sprints.label: Sprint 1
sprints.goal: Read unfamiliar code, repair the health contract and account queries

sprints.label: Sprint 2
sprints.goal: Eliminate broken object-level authorization and injection risks

sprints.label: Sprint 3
sprints.goal: Enforce atomicity, balance checks and safe retries

sprints.label: Sprint 4
sprints.goal: Protect history and logs; produce defensible release evidence

tickets.title: Reproduce the health-check contract regression
tickets.learning: An HTTP endpoint is a contract between a service and its clients. A green process is not necessarily a healthy application. Trace an HTTP request to the service method, write a failing assertion, and preserve response compatibility.
tickets.context: The platform health probe returns 200, but the release dashboard cannot identify the deployed build. On-call asks for a minimal safe fix before rollout.
acceptance: GET /health returns status, service and build fields with the documented values.
No customer data or environment secrets are included in health responses.
Sprint 1 tests pass without disabling an assertion.
tickets.hint: Compare the health contract in the sprint test to the response built in Bank.health().
tickets.reviewPrompt: Why should health endpoints avoid customer data, credentials and stack traces?

tickets.title: Scope and paginate account listings
tickets.learning: Database queries are more than syntax: predicates and limits are part of your API security boundary. Query tenant-owned resources by identity, validate numeric request parameters and test boundary values.
tickets.context: QA reports that the account list occasionally includes customers from other teams, and large accounts pages load unpredictably.
acceptance: Account list returns only rows belonging to the caller-controlled demo identity.
A valid limit restricts results; invalid limits fail safely.
Account IDs have deterministic ordering for tests and consumers.
tickets.hint: Check WHERE owner=? and LIMIT ? together; adding LIMIT without scoping can still leak data.
tickets.reviewPrompt: How would the design change when replacing the demo header with real authentication?

tickets.title: Repair broken object-level authorization
tickets.learning: Object IDs are not authorization. For each read, verify the caller is entitled to the resource. Test an account owner and an unrelated account; avoid leaking sensitive identifiers through failure messages.
tickets.context: A security tester observed that requesting /accounts/2 as alice returned a record belonging to bob.
acceptance: Owner can retrieve the account.
Other actors receive a 403 without account contents.
HTTP contract test reproduces and prevents the regression.
tickets.hint: Find the account first, then compare owner with actor before returning fields.
tickets.reviewPrompt: Why must authorization be enforced server-side even when the UI hides someone else’s account?

tickets.title: Parameterize account search
tickets.learning: Never splice untrusted text into SQL. Parameterized queries separate SQL syntax from data. Apply the tenant authorization predicate before returning records and test adversarial strings.
tickets.context: The accounts-search handler was built in a hurry. A reviewer found string interpolation in its query construction.
acceptance: Search treats strings as data instead of executable SQL.
Results cannot cross the account owner boundary.
Normal search and adversarial search contract tests pass.
tickets.hint: Use ? placeholders and pass values in a tuple; filter by owner in the same query.
tickets.reviewPrompt: What do parameters protect, and what risks remain with dynamically chosen column names?

tickets.title: Enforce atomic transfers and insufficient-funds handling
tickets.learning: A transfer is a single logical unit: debit and credit must commit together or not at all. Use a transaction and protect the account balance invariant. Include ownership checks and concurrency behavior.
tickets.context: Customers report that a failed transfer sometimes subtracts money before raising an error; the payment team wants a root-cause explanation.
acceptance: Insufficient funds and foreign sources are rejected before funds move.
Successful transfers preserve the system-wide total.
No partial debit remains after a failed operation.
tickets.hint: BEGIN IMMEDIATE, check the source balance and owner, and commit both updates in one transaction.
tickets.reviewPrompt: What race arises when two transfers read the same opening balance simultaneously?

tickets.title: Make transfer retries idempotent
tickets.learning: Networks fail after servers commit but before clients receive the response. Clients retry. A payment request must not execute twice when the same key and payload are repeated.
tickets.context: Support found that retrying an interrupted payment duplicated the transfer.
acceptance: A matching retry returns the original transfer ID and does not move funds again.
Reusing the same key with different transfer parameters fails.
The HTTP endpoint distinguishes created (201) from replay (200).
tickets.hint: The UNIQUE(actor,request_key) constraint only helps if you check for an earlier matching row before applying balances.
tickets.reviewPrompt: Why should idempotency keys be scoped by client or account rather than globally?

tickets.title: Fix cross-customer transaction history
tickets.learning: Never assume an endpoint is safe because it is read-only. Restrict result sets with owner-aware joins and write negative access tests.
tickets.context: An audit review discovered an account statement endpoint that could reveal transfer records from unrelated customers.
acceptance: History is scoped to the authenticated owner of each source account.
New customers cannot see the history of an unrelated account.
HTTP tests confirm that empty histories return an empty list.
tickets.hint: Join the transfer source to accounts and bind a.owner to the actor.
tickets.reviewPrompt: What additional access-control decisions apply when a user has joint ownership of an account?

tickets.title: Protect audit logs and publish release evidence
tickets.learning: Log useful security decisions without recording secrets or request bodies. A professional release requires reproducible test evidence, a risk statement, and a code-review-ready change summary.
tickets.context: A reviewer notices tokens and raw transfer request bodies in debug output. The team needs a privacy-safe audit event and a deployment decision.
acceptance: Audit event fields contain bounded, non-sensitive metadata only.
Malformed HTTP transfer payloads produce controlled 4xx errors, not stack traces.
Prepare a PR summary, testing record, risk analysis and deployment/rollback note.
tickets.hint: Whitelist safe audit fields; never serialize whole request dictionaries.
tickets.reviewPrompt: How would you safely correlate events across requests without storing bearer tokens?
